MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 8, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 5:00 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Kevin Shenkman

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:02 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Real Property Negotiator Pursuant t0 Government Code Section 54956.8

  1.  Property Known as The Malibu Lumber Yard (3939 Cross Creek Road APN
  4458-020-903)
  City Negotiator: City Manager Steve McClary or his Designee.
  Negotiating Parties: WPG Malibu LLC, AJS Lumberyard LLC, 9308 Civic
  Center Drive LLC
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:33 p.m.

ROLL CALL
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of July 8, 2024
  Page 2 of 15

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard
  Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBouX, Public
  Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk;
  Kate Manisco, Recreation Manager; Amanda Rigali, Recreation Coordinator; Tracey
  Rossine, Environmental Programs Manager; Fletcher Allen, Associate Planner; Gail
  Duncan, Administrative Assistant; Rebecca Evans, Senior Management Analyst; Salvador
  Lopez, Interim Assistant Flaming Director; and Patricia Salazar, Development and
  Operations Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Lloyd Ahern led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  28, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on July 5, 2024.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8 and 54956.9(d)(l), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action, however
  the Council directed staff to make a report on the school district item.

  Deputy City Attorney Wood reported that after careful consideration and extensive
  mediation efforts the City will resume the petition process initially filed with the Los
  Angeles County Committee on School District Organization in 2017. She stated the City
  remained fully committed to making sure the future Santa Monica Unified School District
  and Malibu Unified School District are allocated sufficient funding to provide a similar
  level of service as before separation. She discussed the importance of communication
  through this process and stated the City will remain transparent and inclusive.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda, hearing the City Manager Updates before Item No. 2.A. and
  adj ourning in memory of Martin Okeke.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  City Council Reorganization

  1.  Presentations to Outgoing Mayor

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart presented the outgoing Mayor award to Mayor
  Uhring.

  Tim Boswell and Roxane made presentations to the outgoing Mayor.

  2.  Remarks by Outgoing Mayor

  Mayor Uhring discussed his term as Mayor and stated he tried to stay true
  to his campaign promises. He thanked City staff including City Clerk
  Pettijohn, the Department Heads, Deputy City Clerk Munoz, Deputy City
  Clerk Lawrence, Senior Management Analyst Ayala, Environmental
  Programs Manager Rossine, and Environmental Health Administrator
  Andico. He thanked the residents for their participation in the City Council
  meetings. He thanked his fellow Councilmembers. He discussed the City’s
  responsibility to preserve and protect Malibu’s resources.

  3.  Election of Mayor

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to nominations for Mayor.

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins second a
  motion to nominate Mayor Pro Tem Stewart for Mayor. The question was
  called, and the motion carried 4-1 , Mayor Pro Tem Stewart abstained.

  4.  Election of Mayor Pro Tem

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to nominations for Mayor Pro Tem.

  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded
  to motion to nominate Councilmember Riggins for Mayor Pro Tem. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

l  5.  Administration of Oath of Office to Newly Elected Mayor and Mayor Pro
l  Tem

  Sharon Stewart administered the Oath of Office to newly elected Mayor
  Stewart

  City Clerk Pettijohn administered the Oath of Office to newly elected
  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins.

  6.  Remarks by Newly Elected Mayor

  Mayor Stewart stated he was proud to serve with Mayor Pro Tem Riggins
  after their election in 2022. He discussed his responsibility to uphold the
  City’s Mission Statement and lead the City as Mayor. He thanked those
  who supported his campaign. He discussed his commitment to representing
  the entire City. He stated the 17th City Council had worked well together
  and discussed the importance of decorum. He stated he would do his best
  to keep the dais focused on City business through the 2024 election cycle.

  B.  Presentation of commendation to Flaming Director Richard Mollica in recognition
  of his service to the City

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins presented the commendation to Flaming Director Mollica.

  Planning Director Mollica thanked the Council for the recognition and stated it had
  been a pleasure serving the City. He discussed his experiences with the City.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary thanked Flaming Director Mollica for his contributions to
  the City. He stated there was an active code enforcement investigation into the July
  4, 2024 event at Nobu. He cautioned the Council that this matter may come before
  them in the future. He stated the City does not have the ability to independently
  shut down events. He discussed the City’ response to and monitoring of the event
  on July 4, 2024. He stated the fatal traffic collision on July 4, 2024 was under
  investigation. He stated Nobu had threatened suit against the City but has not
  served the City with a summons or complaint. He cautioned against discussing this
  matter in open session.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority Ranger, provided the
  Ranger activity report for the last month. He stated 262 parking citations were
  issued, no service calls were generated, and extended patrols were scheduled for
  the July 4, 2024 weekend. He stated rangers closed the parking lot for Escondido
  Trail during road maintenance and assisted in redirecting the public. He stated eight
  administrative citations were issued at Lechuza Beach for possession of alcohol and
  four at Escondido Trail for off-trail use.

  Michel Shane discussed the fatal traffic collision on July 4, 2024. He expressed

Highway (PCH). He commended City officials for working on PCH safety bills in
Sacramento.

Howard Rudzki thanked Planning Director Mollica for his service. He commended
Alicia Peak for her work on the Point Dume Fourth of July parade. He thanked
Seargent Soderlund for his response to illegal fireworks.

Norm Haynie thanked Councilmember Uhring for his service on the City Council
and the Flaming Commission. He commended Mayor Stewart for his skills as a
Councilmember. He commended Planning Director Mollica for his service.

Ryan Embree thanked Councilmember Uhring for his service as Mayor and
congratulated Mayor Stewart; He thanked Planning Director Mollica for his
service. He discussed the event on July 4, 2024 at Nobu and the traffic plan.

Josh Spiegel thanked Councilmember Uhring for his service and congratulated
Mayor Stewart. He thanked Planning Director Mollica for his service. He
discussed the event on July 4, 2024 at Nobu and stated the City need more tools to
shut down unpermitted events.

Skylar Peak thanked the Councilmembers for their service. He thanked Alicia Peak
and the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) volunteers for their work
on the Point Dume Fourth of July parade. He thanked Planning Director Mollica
for his service. He encouraged the City to continue working on PCH safety
programs.
Meril May encouraged the public to report problems in the City to the relevant
agencies so they can be addressed. He discussed bathrooms under construction at
Zuma Beach and Westward Beach. He stated he reported the issue to the County

is an ongoing issue. He discussed traffic impacts from the closure of the Zuma
Beach underpass. He encouraged having more Sheriff s officers. He recommended
purchasing more volunteers on patrol (VOP) vehicles.

Jefferson Wagner thanked the Councilmembers for their service. He presented
pictures of litter on the street near Nobu. He discussed motorhomes continuously
parked near Corral Beach.
Tim Boswell read a portion of a letter from Adrian Fernandez to the City Council.

Roxane read a portion of a letter from Adrian Fernandez to the City Council.

Bill Sampson thanked Councilmember Uhring for his service. He requested the
City look into who could police out of control parties. He stated it was difficult for
residents to get jobs at City Hall. He discussed the alcohol served at the July 4,
2024 event at Nobu and the fatal traffic collision on July 4, 2024. He stated the

  adding medians or removing parking to create a protected bike lane. She stated the

 ALm._ _  4, 2024 weekend and 567 parking citations were issued. He stated SB 1297 had
  been approved by the Privacy and Protection Committee. He thanked Mayor
  Stewart and Deputy City Manager Brown for going to Sacramento and participating
  in the hearing. He stated the bill would be considered by the Appropriations

  Mayor Stewart stated LAZ parking would be able to help with overnight parking
  issues. He discussed meeting decorum and asked the public to hold their applause
  during the meeting.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the City’s prohibition on overnight camping
  and the Supreme Court decision on the Grants Pass v. Johnson case. He encouraged
  the Sheriff’ s Department to enforce the no camping law.

  Captain Jennifer Seetoo, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, discussed the
  fatal traffic collision on July 4, 2024 on PCH. She stated the investigation was
  ongoing and detectives were diligently investigating. She discussed the dangers of
  intoxication and stated the Lost Hills station would start a new program using cafe’
  incident cards to identify where intoxicated individuals were driving from. She

  encouraged the public to report anything they observed or recorded regarding the

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Captain Seetoo stated the cafe' incident
  cards helped identify trends, and the Sheriff s department would work with alcohol
  and beverage control to look at those institutions.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Captain Seetoo stated the Sheriff s
  Department did respond to calls regarding parties. She stated parties in County’s
  jurisdiction are documented and the department works with County Counsel to go
  after the party house. She stated the Sheriff’s Department does not determine if a
  party violated a temporary use permit or conditional use permit.
  Councilmember Uhring thanked Captain Seetoo for the update.

  Captain Seetoo stated the Sheriff’s Department would have a certificate for
  Councilmember Uhring recognizing his service as Mayor. She discussed the
  importance of collaborating with the City and the impact of the speed camera bill.

  Mayor Stewart thanked Captain Seetoo for the update.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, reported crime
  statistics for June 2024. He stated there were 47 Part One crimes and 206 total for
  the year, which is down from last year. He discussed arrests in June 2024, including
  an arrest for possession of narcotics with intent to distribute. He discussed an
  incident on July 3, 2024 where Sheriff s Deputies and Los Angeles County Animal
  Control responded to an incident where a dog had been abandoned and bound by
  zip ties.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund stated there were many
  visitors in Malibu over the holiday weekend.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Silverstein stated he had publicly commented on the July 4, 2024
  event at Nobu on social media. He stated he would consider if he needed to recuse
  himself if the matter eVer came before the Council. He stated the public deserves
  to hear from Council on this tragedy. He discussed traffic collision on July 4, 2024
  and the investigation. He discussed the events on July 4, 2023 and July 4, 2024 at
  Nobu. He read a memo from the City Manager on the conditions staff had put on
  the temporary use permit (TUP) for the July 4, 2024 event. He discussed his
  response to the City Manager and his concern that flnes were not significant enough
  to be a deterrent. He discussed his proposal a year ago to form an Ad Hoc
  Committee to make recommendations on the penalties for unpermitted events. He
  stated the issue had been referred to ZORACES and the committee had not met on
  this issue. He stated residents had submitted correspondence requesting the TUP
  be appealed to the Flaming Commission and discussed the appeal fee which

  elimination of the appeal fee and stated the California Coastal Commission did not
  have an appeal fee. He discussed the TUP condition requiring Public Works
  Departments approval of the traffic plan and the nullification of the permit. He
  discussed how he advocated for emergency enforcement. He discussed the City
  Manager’s memo to the City Council and Sheriff’s Department after the
  nullification of the permit. He discussed evidence that the special event was held
  on July 4, 2024.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin cautioned that this item was not on the agenda and
  should not have an extended discussion.

  Mayor Stewart encouraged Councilmember Silverstein to make his points briefly.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to bring this issue back on an agenda.

  He stated the discussion could be in open or closed session, depending on the

  Councilmember Uhring seconded the motion.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins requested clarification on what information staffwill bring

  Councilmember Silverstein indicated staff should agendize a broad item for the

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated if the Council
  wanted to consider litigation it could be discussed in closed session. He stated he
  did not recommend a general consideration of code enforcement and stated it was
  not generally in the Council’s purview to manage code enforcement on a case-by-

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the CUP could

  City Manager to bring back a report on progress on code enforcement on this

  Councilmember Grisanti indicated support for discussing the threat of litigation in

  City Manager McClary asked the Councilmembers to refrain from discussing staff
  members’ performance.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed social media discourse on this event. He stated

  Councilmember Uhring asked in Ranger Pera had seen the letter from the City of

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, City Manager McClary confirmed the letter

  Councilmember Silverstein stated he read the letter and thought it was very good.

  Councilmember Uhring stated he had spoken with Supervisor Horvath regarding

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins requested additional information on the proposal.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified that ifthe Council wanted to consider sending
  a letter supporting the proposal it would need to be agendized for a future meeting.

  Deputy City Manager Brown discussed the media advisory that was sent out and

  Package proposed by Supervisor’s Linsey Horvath and Janice Hahn, and 2)

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the
  Councilmembers could make brief comments on the issue.

  Councilmember Silverstein indicated support for the proposal.

  Councilmember Grisanti indicated support for expanding the Board of Supervisors.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins indicated support for the proposal.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins announced a weed pulling event at Point Dume headlands

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, City Manager McClary stated information

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated the City would be happy to work with MRCA to

  attended a school district separation mediation meeting and introduced the last

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Interim City Attorney Rusin confirmed

  City Manager McClary suggested adding this item to the work plan discussion. He

  Mayor Stewart commended Alicia Peak for her work on the Point Dume Fourth of
  July parade. He discussed the limited staffing in law enforcement and it was not a
  matter of funding. He stated he attended the Cruise Malibu campaign launch. He
  stated he attended the Privacy and Protection Committee hearing on the PCH safety

  the Grants Pass V. Johnson decision and stated it allowed another tool in the toolbox
